newsitem.title: KENYA: Eastern Zaire town reported besieged by rebels.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Zaire town reported besieged by rebels.

text.p: Rebels are besieging the eastern Zairean town of Kindu but appear to be holding off attacking the heavily fortified base to allow as many civilians as possible to leave, a regional military source said on Thursday.

The source, who closely monitors the war pitting Laurent Kabila's rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire against Zaire's army, said morale among government troops was low and panic had set in among them.
In Nairobi, the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said it was diverting food aid for displaced people and refugees from a route via Kindu to Ilebo 600 km (375 miles) away for security reasons.

WFP spokeswoman Brenda Barton told Reuters that relief cargo would now be moved first by railway from Lubumbashi, the capital of mineral-rich Shaba province, to Ilebo and then by river from Ilebo to Kisangani for some 170,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees.
The diversion means an extra delay of two weeks and it will now take the agency five weeks to move food from its import source in Zambia to Kisangani, she said.
"The diversion is necessary because operators in Kindu can no longer guarantee safety of the relief cargo there," she said.
Another U.N. aid worker said security had sharply deteriorated in Kindu. "Obviously things are getting worse there in Kindu because everyone seems to be running away," he said.
Kindu, a key transport hub on the Zaire River and declared a target by Kabila, is the northernmost working station on a rail line to South Africa. It also has a large airport used by the military.

"The town is besieged and rebels are within reach. They (rebels) could take it if they wanted to but strategy appears to centre around allowing as many civilians as possible to escape," the regional military source told Reuters.
"They want to portray themselves as the good guys so they want minimum casualties when they storm Kindu," he added.
On Wednesday, officials of Zaire's Cizarail train company in the capital Kinshasa said they suspended all traffic to Kindu and evacuated staff and equipment in case of rebel attack.
Cizarail sources said the town was deserted on Tuesday and its residents had fled.
A Cizarail director in Kinshasa said there had been no radio contact with the town since Tuesday, after materials and some personnel were evacuated.
"Since all the other services had evacuated we too followed. It is a preventive measure to protect our materials," he said.
Cizarail is owned partly by Belgian and South African interests and partly by the Zairean state. It is a vital route for mining exports and food and other imports to the southeast.
Zaire's defence ministry said on Wednesday it had beaten back a rebel advance on the town, killing hundreds of rebels in an ambush 35 km (22 miles) further east.

But the regional military source on Thursday denied the report, saying Kabila's rebel force had met no major military hurdles in their advance towards Kindu from the town of Kalima 80 km (50 miles) away which they captured last Sunday.

He said morale among Zairean government troops in Kindu appeared "very low and panic set in after the Kindu governor fled the town early this week". Kinshasa says the governor had left the town for a pre-arranged meeting in the capital.
The source said some aircraft and heavy equipment had been removed from Kindu and mercenaries had departed from the formerly heavily fortified army and air base near the town.
